practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution explicitly mentions the freedom of speech in Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 105 of the Indian Constitution deals with the powers, privileges, and immunities of Parliament and its members. Clause (1) of Article 105 guarantees freedom of speech in Parliament. Article 194 deals with state legislatures.

practiceQuestions.q: Freedom of speech and expression available to a Member of Parliament (MP) inside the House is subject to:
opts: Provisions of the Constitution and the rules and standing orders of the House
Prior approval of the Speaker or Chairman
Judicial review by the Supreme Court
practiceQuestions.sol: The freedom of speech available to MPs under Article 105(1) is subject to the provisions of the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating the procedure of Parliament, not the reasonable restrictions of Article 19(2).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the duration of immunity from arrest for members of Parliament in civil cases?
opts: 40 days before and 40 days after the session
14 days before and 14 days after the session
Only during the days the House is actually sitting
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Section 135A of the Code of Civil Procedure, MPs are exempt from arrest in civil cases during the continuance of the meeting of the House, and for 40 days before and 40 days after such meeting.

practiceQuestions.q: Are MPs immune from arrest in criminal cases or cases of preventive detention?
opts: Yes, for all criminal matters during sessions
No, immunity is available only for civil cases
Yes, with prior permission of the President of India
Yes, if the crime is committed within the Parliament premises
practiceQuestions.sol: The privilege of freedom from arrest is limited only to civil cases. MPs have no immunity from arrest in criminal cases, preventive detention, or contempt of court.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies or authorities decides whether a breach of parliamentary privilege has occurred?
opts: The Privileges Committee or the House itself
practiceQuestions.sol: Each House of Parliament is the sole judge of any breach of its privileges or contempt. It can punish individuals through its Privileges Committee or by a direct resolution of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a Member of Parliament be compelled to give evidence as a witness in a court of law without the leave of the House?
opts: No, they have complete exemption as witnesses during a session
Yes, provided the Supreme Court issues a warrant
No, the exemption applies only to criminal trials
practiceQuestions.sol: MPs have the freedom from being summoned as a witness in a court of law while Parliament is in session, without the leave (permission) of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional article specifies the privileges of state legislatures and their members equivalent to Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 194 of the Constitution deals with the powers, privileges, and immunities of the State Legislatures, their committees, and their members, closely mirroring Article 105 for Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: What protection does an MP enjoy regarding statements made or votes cast in Parliament?
opts: Immunity from any liability in any court for anything said or voted
Protection only if approved by the Ethics Committee
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 105(2), no member of Parliament shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given by him in Parliament or any committee thereof.

practiceQuestions.q: Before the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, parliamentary privileges in India were equated with those of which foreign legislative body?
practiceQuestions.sol: Originally, Article 105(3) stated that parliamentary privileges would be those of the British House of Commons as of 1950 until defined by Parliament. The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed this reference to the House of Commons.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is NOT categorized as an individual parliamentary privilege?
opts: Freedom from arrest in civil cases
Right to regulate the procedure of the House
Exemption from attendance as a witness
practiceQuestions.sol: The right to regulate the procedure and conduct business of the House is a collective privilege enjoyed by the House as a whole, not an individual member privilege.

practiceQuestions.q: How do individual parliamentary privileges balance the principle of legislative independence with the rule of law?
opts: By placing MPs completely above the jurisdiction of all courts permanently
By granting immunity only for official legislative duties to enable fearless debate, while subjecting MPs to general laws outside the House
By allowing the judiciary to dictate parliamentary debates and speech contents
By giving executive veto powers over individual MP utterances
practiceQuestions.sol: Individual privileges protect MPs from legal consequences for actions/words inside the legislature, ensuring fearless representation, but these privileges do not exempt them from criminal law, ordinary civil liabilities outside the defined session windows, or constitutional boundaries, thereby preserving the rule of law.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the rationale behind omitting the direct reference to the British House of Commons in Article 105(3) via the 44th Amendment Act?
opts: To abolish all parliamentary privileges completely
To eliminate colonial legacies and align constitutional text with national dignity and self-reliance in legislative interpretation
To transfer the power of defining privileges solely to the Supreme Court
To merge parliamentary privileges with fundamental rights under Part III
practiceQuestions.sol: Retaining a reference to a foreign legislature was seen as a colonial baggage unbecoming of an independent democratic republic. The 44th Amendment ensured that privileges would be those that existed prior to the amendment, while empowering Parliament to codify them.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Supreme Court's ruling in the P.V. Narasimha Rao case (1998) impact individual parliamentary privileges regarding bribery?
opts: It held that MPs accepting bribes to vote are immune from prosecution under Article 105(2)
It completely abolished immunity of speech inside Parliament
It declared all individual privileges unconstitutional
It gave the executive branch powers to arrest MPs during sessions
practiceQuestions.sol: In the P.V. Narasimha Rao case (1998), the Supreme Court held that MPs who took bribes to vote in Parliament enjoyed immunity from criminal prosecution under Article 105(2) if they actually cast the vote. (Note: This was later partially overturned by a 7-judge bench in 2024, but historically 1998 established this protective interpretation of the privilege).

practiceQuestions.q: Can an MP claim immunity from arrest in civil cases if they are attending a committee meeting of Parliament during a recess?
opts: No, committee meetings are not part of parliamentary sessions
Yes, immunity applies to days when the House or its committees meet, plus the 40-day buffer period
Only if the Privileges Committee explicitly grants a special order
No, immunity applies strictly when the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha is in plenary session
practiceQuestions.sol: The civil arrest immunity extends not only when the House sits in plenary session, but also when committees of Parliament meet, covering the operational continuity of parliamentary business.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are individual privileges considered essential despite potential perceptions of elite impunity?
opts: To enable legislators to hold the executive accountable without fear of malicious litigation or intimidation
To allow MPs to bypass ordinary tax and civil laws permanently
To prevent police forces from ever entering the national capital territory
To grant MPs absolute immunity from criminal offences
practiceQuestions.sol: Privileges are not designed to place MPs above the law for personal benefit, but to protect them from external coercion, executive overreach, or frivolous litigation so they can speak and act freely on behalf of citizens.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional status regarding codification of parliamentary privileges in India?
opts: Privileges must compulsorily be codified by a constitutional amendment
Parliament has chosen not to codify them comprehensively, preferring to rely on uncodified British House of Commons traditions and parliamentary precedents
The Supreme Court has banned Parliament from ever passing a codification law
Privileges were fully codified in a single statute in 1952
practiceQuestions.sol: Although Article 105(3) permitted Parliament to define its privileges by law, Parliament has never enacted a comprehensive code. It relies instead on British precedents, rules of the House, and judicial interpretations.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the privilege of freedom of speech interact with the publication of parliamentary proceedings?
opts: Publishing parliamentary debates is illegal unless done by government media
True reports of parliamentary proceedings published under authority are protected, shielding publishers from civil/criminal action
Publishers face automatic contempt of court if they quote an MP
Media outlets enjoy the exact same absolute personal immunity as MPs inside the well of the House
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 361A (inserted by the 44th Amendment), no person shall be liable in any court for publishing a substantially true report of either House's proceedings, unless proved to be published with malice, protecting free flow of legislative information.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the legal boundary between internal parliamentary proceedings and judicial review in India?
opts: Courts can review every single debate and procedural motion inside Parliament
Courts cannot inquire into parliamentary proceedings on the ground of alleged irregularity of procedure, but can examine unconstitutionality or gross illegality
Judicial review has zero application to anything happening in the capital
The Speaker's decision on all matters is final and immune from judicial review under any circumstance
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 122 protects internal proceedings from being challenged in court on procedural irregularity grounds. However, the Supreme Court has clarified that if proceedings are unconstitutional, blatantly illegal, or violate fundamental rights fundamentally, judicial review can apply.

practiceQuestions.q: How are breaches of individual privileges handled when a non-member (outsider) criticizes or obstructs an MP?
opts: The matter must be referred directly to a local police station FIR
The House can summon the offender at its bar, reprimand, admonish, or imprison them for contempt of the House
Outsiders possess absolute immunity against any parliamentary action
The MP must personally file a defamation suit in a civil court only
practiceQuestions.sol: A breach of privilege or contempt of the House by an outsider can be tried by the House itself. The House possesses penal powers, including admonition, reprimand, or commitment to custody (prison) for a specified duration.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the interplay between fundamental rights (e.g., Article 19 and Article 21) and parliamentary privileges?
opts: Fundamental rights always override parliamentary privileges in every context
Both are part of the Constitution; harmonious construction is applied, though Article 105 privileges operate as specific constitutional provisions
Parliamentary privileges completely nullify Part III of the Constitution
Article 21 has no application to any person inside Parliament House
practiceQuestions.sol: Courts have held that since both privileges and fundamental rights are constitutional provisions, they must be harmoniously interpreted. However, specific provisions like Article 105 override general fundamental rights like Article 19(1)(a) inside the House contextually.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding individual parliamentary privileges in India:
1. The freedom of speech available to a member of Parliament is absolute and not subject to any internal rules or standing orders of the House.
2. An MP cannot be prosecuted in any court for anything said during a parliamentary committee meeting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because freedom of speech under Article 105(1) is explicitly subject to the provisions of the Constitution and the rules and standing orders of the House. Statement 2 is correct as Article 105(2) extends immunity to anything said or votes given in Parliament or any committee thereof.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding immunity from arrest for members of Parliament:
1. The immunity from arrest covers both civil and criminal cases equally throughout the year.
2. In criminal cases or preventive detention, an MP can be arrested even while Parliament is in session without needing the Speaker's permission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because immunity from arrest applies strictly to civil cases, not criminal cases or preventive detention. Statement 2 is correct; MPs have no arrest immunity in criminal/preventive detention cases and can be arrested like ordinary citizens, though the arresting authority must inform the Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the evolution of parliamentary privileges in India:
1. The original text of the Indian Constitution contained a direct reference linking parliamentary privileges to those of the British House of Commons.
2. The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 completely removed the reference to the British House of Commons from Article 105.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 105(3) originally equated privileges with those of the British House of Commons. The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 amended this clause to substitute that reference with powers, privileges, and immunities as they existed immediately before the coming into force of Section 26 of the 44th Amendment.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the exemption of MPs from serving as witnesses:
1. An MP can be compelled to attend a court as a witness during an ongoing session of Parliament without the House's permission.
2. This exemption is designed to ensure that parliamentary business is not disrupted by the absence of members attending judicial proceedings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because MPs enjoy freedom from being summoned as a witness while Parliament is in session without the leave of the House. Statement 2 is correct as the fundamental objective is legislative continuity and non-obstruction of duties.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the publication of parliamentary proceedings:
1. Under Article 361A, no civil or criminal proceedings can be initiated against a person for publishing a substantially true report of parliamentary proceedings.
2. This protection applies even if the report of the proceedings was published with express malice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct under Article 361A. Statement 2 is incorrect because the protection under Article 361A does NOT apply to a report published with malice (ill will).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the privileges of state legislature members under Article 194:
1. The privileges of members of state legislatures are automatically identical in scope to those of members of Parliament under Article 105.
2. State legislatures have the power to punish non-members for contempt of the House in the same manner as Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 194(3) states that the powers, privileges, and immunities of a House of a State Legislature and its members shall be those of Parliament and its members, until defined by the state legislature. Both have contempt penal powers over outsiders.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the limits of individual parliamentary privileges:
1. Parliamentary privileges can be used by an MP to commit defamation against a private citizen outside the floor of the House without legal recourse.
2. An MP arrested on a criminal charge inside Parliament premises without prior permission of the Speaker violates constitutional privilege directly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false because speech outside the House (e.g., in press conferences) does not enjoy Article 105 immunity. Statement 2 is false because criminal arrest inside Parliament premises requires intimation to the Speaker, but criminal/preventive detention immunity does not exist anywhere, and arrests within precincts require permission of the presiding officer only per convention, but legally criminal immunity is non-existent.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the enforcement and adjudication of parliamentary privileges:
1. The Supreme Court of India has the final authority to determine the existence and scope of parliamentary privileges if a dispute arises.
2. Parliamentary privileges are superior to Fundamental Rights in all conceivable scenarios.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; under the Indian constitutional framework, the judiciary (Supreme Court) is the final interpreter of the Constitution, including the scope of Article 105. Statement 2 is incorrect; privileges do not automatically override fundamental rights unconditionally (e.g., Article 21 can intersect in high-stakes liberty disputes).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the civil arrest immunity window for MPs:
1. The 40-day immunity period applies before and after the adjournment of the House or prorogation.
2. This immunity extends to debts incurred by the MP in their private business capacity as well as public official capacity without distinction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (40 days before and 40 days after the session). Statement 2 is incorrect because the civil arrest immunity under Section 135A CPC applies only to civil process/debt arrests, but does not provide permanent shield against execution of decrees in all arbitrary private fraud contexts where statutory exceptions or specific court processes apply, nor does it override clear statutory limits on criminal/fraudulent liabilities.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historical classification and nature of privileges:
1. Parliamentary privileges are divided broadly into individual privileges and collective privileges.
2. Individual privileges cease to exist the moment a member loses their seat due to disqualification or dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Parliamentary privileges are categorized into individual and collective privileges. Furthermore, individual privileges are meant to protect members *while* they are serving as members; upon cessation of membership (dissolution, resignation, disqualification), individual privileges no longer attach to that person.
